solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boss put right on mistake

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed on the end of the word for the mistake

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A manager corrects an error someone has made.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British slang for a boss or foreman, also a football manager.

clue.text: An account of lost island

parts.note: a toll is the count of those lost, as in a death toll

explanation.surface: A story about a lost island, the stuff of adventure tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral reef ring enclosing a lagoon is a kind of island.

clue.text: Are they still living together?

parts.note: reads like gossip about a couple, but still can mean flat (motionless or level) and living together suggests mates sharing a home

explanation.surface: A nosy question about whether a couple are still a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: 'still' is FLAT, as in level or not fizzy, and 'living together' is MATES, so it describes sharers of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: People who share a rented apartment live together without being a couple.

clue.text: Guy with decorative strip

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them, as is to rib them
and means together with

explanation.surface: A man wearing a decorative ribbon or sash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man but is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A riband is an old spelling of ribbon, a narrow decorative band of fabric.

clue.text: Extremely cool and dry where ants are found

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered
ants live in a nest

explanation.surface: Describes a calm, arid spot where an ants' colony lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of calm or unruffled, so most cool in temperament.

clue.text: One who expects to be paid

definitions.text: One who expects to be paid

parts.words: One who expects to be paid
parts.note: sounds like a creditor or worker, but expects means is expecting a baby, carried on another's behalf for a fee

explanation.surface: Someone waiting for their wages or a debt to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expects' in the sense of being pregnant is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who carries a baby for another couple, sometimes paid for doing so.

clue.text: Artist only out of place in Liverpool?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the nickname of the club

parts.note: Liverpool Football Club are nicknamed the Reds

indicators.note: letters out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist feeling uniquely out of his element in the city of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool here is the football club, whose red shirts give it the nickname used in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was a leading 18th-century English portrait painter.

clue.text: Renoir work featuring tip of girl's elbow

indicators.note: the painting has the girl's tip within it

parts.note: Renoir famously painted many nudes

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Renoir painting showing the point of a young woman's elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elbow' is a verb here, not the joint in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push them gently with the arm, a prod.

clue.text: Running race vest on male (this one?)

definitions.text: Running race vest on male (this one?)

indicators.note: the male letter is placed after the rearranged letters
running in the sense of liquid or melting, so the letters flow into a new order

parts.note: the fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A runner in a race vest, and the clue asks whether this is the man himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a famous British middle-distance runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Cram was a British world-record-breaking miler of the 1980s, a male runner in a racing vest.

clue.text: Fruit began going off in truck

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the vehicle

parts.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

indicators.note: going off suggests turning bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit spoiling while still in the delivery truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' reads naturally as the fruit rotting, which is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between a raspberry and a blackberry, a soft berry.

clue.text: Coming second in Olympic contest

parts.note: due means expected or coming, as in a payment due

indicators.note: the second letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Finishing runner-up in an Olympic event.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or contest between two parties, originally with weapons.

clue.text: A bird very much after love? On the contrary

indicators.note: with the next phrase, this sets the order of the two pieces
reverses the stated order, so love comes after the intensifier rather than before it

parts.note: flaming is an intensifier, meaning extremely
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird is fiercely in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very much after love' would put O first; 'On the contrary' flips it so O goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: Foretold 'geezers' appearing in dictionary

indicators.note: the men go inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
geezer is British slang for a man, so geezers are men

explanation.surface: A slang word, quoted, has been predicted to enter the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To omen something is to portend or prophesy it.

clue.text: Angled, no line is doing that

indicators.note: means the line letter is removed

parts.note: atilt means tilted, at an angle

explanation.surface: Something tilted that is not lined up properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at it is to be busy doing something, the something already mentioned.

clue.text: Crossing party-goer, ending up outside

indicators.note: the turned word wraps round the partygoer
in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: last means final, the ending
a raver is someone who goes to raves or parties

explanation.surface: A partygoer crossing over, ending up outside the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending up' looks like a phrase meaning finishing, but 'up' reverses the word for ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is an act of going across something.

clue.text: Hearing car, attempt to cross over

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: the attempt crosses over the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Listening for a car as one tries to get across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives describing things to do with the sense of listening.

clue.text: 1 purse over part of hand

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 1 across, defined there as boss

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a prize fund or purse
a hand is a bunch of bananas, so one fruit is part of it

explanation.surface: A cryptic reference to money and a hand, built around a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns POT round. A hand is a cluster of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the most important person, the boss, matching 1 across.

clue.text: Fire more effectively moved us to scream

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted about

parts.note: a scream, something very funny, is a hoot

explanation.surface: Someone was so moved they were driven to scream.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshoot is to shoot better than a rival.

clue.text: Extensive energy consumption to produce rubber?

parts.note: mass means large-scale, as in mass production
use is consumption

explanation.surface: Huge energy use needed to manufacture rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' is not the material but someone who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages rubs her clients, so she is a rubber.

clue.text: Go over start of marriage ceremony

indicators.note: the burst word is placed over, around, the opening letter

parts.note: to go pop is to burst, so pop means go

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rehearsing the opening of a wedding service.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour or display.

clue.text: War god admitting cook is lover

indicators.note: the god lets the cooking word inside

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: The god of war confesses that the cook is his lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves something fondly is a lover of it, a fan.

clue.text: Messenger's carried in another message

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s is a contraction of is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the next words

explanation.surface: A courier's letter is enclosed inside a further letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god who carried messages for the other gods.

clue.text: Help them to overturn vehicles

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturning reads the letters upwards

parts.note: aid is help
em is a colloquial short form of them

explanation.surface: An instruction to help some people flip cars over.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels of communication, such as newspapers, serve as vehicles for ideas.

clue.text: In retreat, also run in after weapons

indicators.note: the run letter and the turned word go inside the word for after together

parts.note: once can mean after, as in once you finish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so this word reads in reverse

parts.note: and means also

explanation.surface: A soldier, retreating, also runs in after collecting the weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is not positional here: ONCE means after, as in 'once you have eaten'. 'In retreat' turns the word for also round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means military weapons and supplies, artillery in particular.

clue.text: Plastered adult cuts deck, shuffling

indicators.note: the adult letter cuts into the mixed letters
shuffling a deck mixes its letters

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A drunk grown-up cutting and shuffling a pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffling' turns DECK into CKED, which A cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: Caked means thickly coated, as with mud or plaster.

clue.text: American education is no stranger

definitions.note: being familiar with something, as in accustomed to it

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with the American school system.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accustomed to something means one is no stranger to it.

clue.text: Slip into TA, chasing old soldiers

indicators.note: the second part follows after the letter for old
the slip goes inside the word of gratitude

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
to slip is to err

explanation.surface: A soldier slips into the Territorial Army after old soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: TA looks like the Territorial Army but is 'ta', British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Other ranks are all soldiers who are not commissioned officers.

clue.text: Tree, also wild olive

indicators.note: wild suggests uncontrolled, so the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Naming a tree that also goes by wild olive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' looks like the definition, but it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a shrub known as the wild olive or Russian olive.

clue.text: Useful, as chaser for second drink

indicators.note: a chaser follows another drink, so the useful word comes after the letter

parts.note: handy means useful

explanation.surface: A useful tip that one drink can chase another.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink.
